statement.p: Find the equation (in terms of x and y) of the tangent line to the curve r=2\sin5\theta at \theta=\pi/3.

static.solution: x and y as being parametrically equations with parameter \theta: x = r\cos(\theta) = 2 \sin(5\theta) \cos(\theta), \ \hbox{and}\ y = r\sin(\theta) = 2 \sin(5\theta) \sin(\theta). Then we know that the slope of the tangent line is {dy\over dx} = {dy/d\theta\over dx/d\theta}. Taking the derivatives, {dx\over d\theta} = 2(5\cos(5\theta)\cos(\theta) - \sin(5\theta)\sin(\theta)) and {dy\over d\theta} = 2(5\cos(5\theta)\sin(\theta) + \sin(5\theta)\cos(\theta)). Thus {dy\over dx} = {5\cos(5\theta)\sin(\theta) + \sin(5\theta)\cos(\theta) \over 5\cos(5\theta)\cos(\theta) - \sin(5\theta)\sin(\theta) }. We want this at \theta = \pi/3, so that we get {dy\over dx}\approx 0.866. Then, at \theta = \pi/3, x(\pi/3) = 2 \sin(5\cdot \pi/3)\cos(\pi/3) \approx -0.866, and y(\pi/3) = 2 \sin(5\cdot \pi/3)\sin(\pi/3) \approx -1.5, so that the tangent line is y \approx -1.5 + (0.866)(x + 0.866). (Note, however, that the correct answer may require more significant figures than are shown in this solution.)
